message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 180, "amount_cents": 13791}, {"order_id": 181, "amount_cents": 17092}, {"order_id": 184, "amount_cents": 3930}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Alpha's handoff says refunds are done, but I need to verify the ledger before paying anyone. I'll start by checking the refunds list against the three reported refunds.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 180, 181, and 184 with the same amounts. Next I'll pull the orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself, starting with acme.
acme's net_cents of 13345 matches my check: orders 180 and 183 total 27136, minus refund 180 (13791). Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance.
birch's net_cents of 19909 matches my check: orders 181 and 184 total 40931, minus refunds 181 (17092) and 184 (3930) gives 19909. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its net balance next to confirm.

Cobalt's net_cents of 31469 matches my check: orders 182 and 185 total 31469 with no refunds. All three balances match my independent check and the refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme at 13345.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance (19909) matches my independent check from the orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's net balance of 31469 matches my independent check from orders 182 and 185 with no refunds. Recording the last payout.
All three payouts are recorded and the total checks out: payouts sum to 64723, which equals order total 99536 minus refunds 34813. The task is complete.
